source.paper_title: Star-quadtrees and guard-quadtrees: I/O-efficient indexes for fat triangulations and low-density planar subdivisions
source.sections: §2.1 stopping rule; §2.2 Z-order and cell-triangle records; §2.3 direct top-down construction and per-vertex-star I/O-efficient construction

contract.operation: Construct the ordinary Star quadtree for a bounded fat triangulation of the square by recursively splitting any cell whose intersecting triangulation edges do not all share a common vertex, then emit every leaf-cell/triangle intersection keyed by the leaf's Z-order interval start.
contract.profile_scope: The frame accepts exactly the two diagonal triangulations of the canonical square and its four-triangle center fan. The profile measures the Star stopping rule and linear-quadtree cell-triangle representation; it does not measure arbitrary triangulation validation, per-vertex-star external-memory bulk construction, or B-tree construction.
contract.coordinate_system: The canonical square is [0,8] x [0,8], with vertices 0=(0,0), 1=(8,0), 2=(8,8), 3=(0,8); the optional fifth vertex 4=(4,4). Coordinates use x rightward and y upward.
contract.fatness: Every accepted triangle has angles 45,45,90 degrees and is therefore 45-degree fat under the paper's minimum-angle definition.
contract.cell_rule: Edges intersect closed canonical squares. A cell stops if it has no intersecting edge or every intersecting edge has one shared endpoint. Otherwise split into NW, NE, SW, SE children in that order.
contract.depth_overflow: A non-stopping cell at depth 2 is invalid. For the three accepted square triangulations, every nonincident edge pair is separated by at least 4 coordinate units, while a depth-2 cell's diagonal is 2*sqrt(2), so this cap contains the complete stopping subdivision.
contract.z_key: The integer Morton start key at fixed depth 2. Interleave top-origin row bits before x bits, matching the paper's Z-index convention and NW,NE,SW,SE order. A shallower leaf uses the first key in its depth-2 interval.
contract.output_encoding: Little-endian signed i64 words [pair_count, z_key, triangle_id, ...]. Emit one pair for each closed leaf-cell/triangle intersection; pairs are sorted by z_key then input triangle ID. The canonical square is fully triangulated, so every leaf has at least one triangle pair.

workspace.meaning: Fixed vertex, triangle, unique-edge, and cell-triangle pair arrays plus bounded recursion state; caller input and output buffers are excluded.
